fc32.name: Swale on contour (from elevation), spillway south
fc32.notes: Suggested: set out the level line on site with an A-frame after a wet season of watching. From the 5 m elevation the level line here is about 119 m and runs north–south between the house and cabin. The bench sits on a spur, so only about 0.1 ha drains to it: the boggy patch is more likely seepage or poorly draining clay. Spill at the south end into the rain garden, never toward the house.
fc32.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc33.name: Swale spillway
fc33.notes: Suggested: rock-lined spillway from the swale end to the rain garden.
fc33.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc34.name: Rain garden / overflow basin
fc34.notes: Suggested: mulched basin with water-tolerant plants (Lomandra, native ginger, bananas at its edge) that takes the swale and tank overflows.
fc34.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc35.name: Privacy screen on the swale berm (under 2 m)
fc35.notes: Suggested species under about 2 m: native ginger, cordyline, lilly pilly hedge kept clipped, finger lime, midyim. Keeps morning sun on the house.
fc35.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc36.name: Garden tank on the high side (proposed)
fc36.notes: Suggested: a garden tank at about 121 m, fed by the cabin roof and topped up from the shed. About 3–4 m above the vegetable beds gives about 30 kPa for drip and soaker lines.
fc36.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc37.name: Garden tank to vegetable beds
fc37.notes: Suggested: 25 mm poly from the garden tank to the beds and the chicken waterer.
fc37.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc38.name: Raised or wicking beds over the clay
fc38.notes: Suggested: start with 3–4 beds (about 30–50 m²) on raised or wicking beds over the clay, after a soil test that includes arsenic and organochlorines (old banana land).
fc38.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc39.name: Soil test: vegetable patch
fc39.notes: Suggested: lab soil test plus arsenic and organochlorine screen before growing vegetables (NSW EPA names arsenic and dieldrin as the main leftovers on old banana land).
fc39.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc40.name: Soil test: orchard
fc40.notes: Suggested: standard lab test; 10–15 cores mixed.
fc40.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc41.name: Soil test and infiltration: boggy patch
fc41.notes: Suggested: test the boggy ground by the driveway (slake and infiltration tests too) to see whether it is seepage, compaction or sodic clay.
fc41.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc42.name: Soil test: chicken run
fc42.notes: Suggested: screen the chicken run too, as chickens forage in the soil.
fc42.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc43.name: Mango guild
fc43.notes: Suggested guild: mulched to 1 m from the trunk; comfrey and turmeric at the drip line; pigeon pea outside it on the north, cut twice a year; ginger, arrowroot and sweet potato between trees; bananas on the sunny edge with greywater.
fc43.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc44.name: Laundry greywater to bananas and citrus
fc44.notes: Suggested: a greywater diverter from the laundry to a mulched banana circle; not on leafy greens; keep clear of the septic field (location to confirm) and check council rules.
fc44.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc45.name: Macadamia (local native)
fc45.notes: Suggested: native to the region; canopy layer of the food forest extension.
fc45.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc47.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc48.name: Low-chill peach (netted)
fc48.notes: Group addition: net or bag against Queensland fruit fly.
fc48.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc49.name: Custard apple / atemoya
fc49.notes: Group addition: frost-tender, keep on the bench.
fc49.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc50.name: Davidson's plum (local native)
fc50.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc51.name: Finger lime (local native)
fc51.notes: Suggested native understorey; thorny, good near the chicken run edge.
fc51.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc52.name: Midyim (local native)
fc52.notes: Group addition; good under the citrus edge.
fc52.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc53.name: Grumichama (check label: Eugenia brasiliensis)
fc53.notes: Group addition; make sure it is not Surinam or Brazilian cherry (E. uniflora).
fc53.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc54.name: Native stingless bee hive
fc54.notes: Suggested: Tetragonula hive at the orchard edge, morning sun and afternoon shade. Honey bees need NSW DPI registration.
fc54.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc55.name: Low-fuel zone round the house and cabin
fc55.notes: Suggested: keep fuel low here (mown lawn, irrigated gardens, no lantana or dense dry shrubs). Check NSW bushfire-prone land mapping and Planning for Bush Fire Protection.
fc55.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc56.name: Fire approach (W–NW, upslope from the creek)
fc56.notes: Suggested sector: hot dry westerlies in late winter–spring, and fire runs fastest upslope from the creek.
fc56.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc57.name: Winter westerlies (check)
fc57.notes: Suggested to check: cold dry westerlies are common inland of the coast in winter and spring. Confirm with the Lismore wind roses and observation.
fc57.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc58.name: Correction: sun angles
fc58.notes: The draft sector diagram has the angles swapped: winter sunrise about 63°, sunset about 297°; summer sunrise about 117°, sunset about 243° (at about 28.6° S).
fc58.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc59.name: Zone 3 · creek flats and lower west slope
fc59.notes: Suggested: flood-prone flats and the lower slope: pasture for a few sheep, flood-tolerant trees, a possible pond site out of flood reach. Cold air settles here: no frost-tender trees.
fc59.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc60.name: Zone 4 · lower forested slopes
fc60.notes: Suggested: managed bush and lower slopes: lantana control from the good bush outward, firewood, a trail on contour.
fc60.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc61.name: Zone 5 · upper bush (habitat and corridor)
fc61.notes: Suggested: steep forest (over a third of the property is steeper than 50%). Habitat, corridor, Land for Wildlife; possible conservation agreement.
fc61.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc62.name: Creek riparian buffer (at least 10–20 m)
fc62.notes: Suggested: no cultivation, stock camping or fertiliser along the creek; riparian planting may get Landcare support.
fc62.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc63.name: Water-powered creek pump (option)
fc63.notes: Long-term option: a ram or Bunyip pump on the permanent creek lifting water about 24 m to a header tank above the gardens. Try the Ram & Bunyip pumps tool. Domestic and stock use only unless licensed.
fc63.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)

fc64.name: Bush walking trail on contour (idea)
fc64.notes: Long-term idea: a walking or bike trail on contour with drainage turnouts every 20–30 m.
fc64.source: Review suggestion (Firefly Farm design review, 23 Oct 2026)
